presentation.title: Unauthorized External Account Linking
presentation.summary: Practice responding to unfamiliar microdeposits, a linked external account, a verification call, and a pending bank-to-bank transfer.
presentation.practiceGoal: Recognize that tiny deposits can be part of account-link verification, refuse to confirm them for an unexpected caller, and review every access and money-movement setting with the real bank.

warningSigns.sign: Two tiny deposits appear from an institution you do not recognize.
An external bank account is linked without your permission.
An unexpected caller asks for the exact microdeposit amounts.
A pending ACH transfer goes to the unfamiliar external account.
A cancellation link requests online-banking credentials or another security code.

finalReview.safestAction: Open the bank app or website you already trust, inspect linked accounts, and contact the bank immediately about any link or transfer you did not authorize.

realWorldActions.action: Do not tell an unexpected caller the exact microdeposit amounts and do not send a test payment to an unfamiliar account.
Ask the real bank to lock or remove unauthorized links and review pending transfers while they are still pending.
Review linked accounts, active devices, sessions, contact details, payees, and recent transactions together.
Ignore caller-supplied cancellation forms. Continue only through the trusted bank channel.
If the bank recommends account replacement, use its transition plan for Social Security deposits, pensions, bills, and other legitimate activity. Recovery outcomes vary.

artifact.heading: External-account activity
artifact.message: The known bank app shows deposits of $0.07 and $0.13 from an unfamiliar institution. A notice says an external account was added.
artifact.transcript: The simulated known bank app shows two small deposits, one for seven cents and one for thirteen cents, from an unfamiliar institution. A notice says an external account was added. A microdeposit is a tiny amount sometimes used to confirm access to an account. An external account is an account at another financial institution linked for bank-to-bank transfers.

scene.question: Are the amounts too small to matter?
scene.description: Tiny amounts can be the setup step for a much larger unauthorized transfer.

warningSigns.sign: The learner does not recognize the depositing institution.
The learner did not add an external account.
Two small deposits may be part of a verification process.

choice.title: Inspect linked accounts in the known app
choice.subtitle: Treat the small entries as possible setup activity.

feedback.heading: You looked beyond the small dollar amounts
feedback.consequence: The unfamiliar link can be reviewed before a larger transfer is completed.
feedback.explanation: The size of a microdeposit does not measure the size of the risk it may be verifying.

warningSigns.sign: The external-account notice was not expected.

choice.title: Make a note and wait for the statement
choice.subtitle: Review the entries at the end of the month.

feedback.heading: You noticed the entries but delayed the account review
feedback.consequence: The external link may become active while the learner waits.
feedback.explanation: Unknown account-link activity deserves prompt attention even when the amounts are only a few cents.

warningSigns.sign: The notice says a new external account exists now.

choice.title: Ignore the deposits because they added money
choice.subtitle: Assume a positive amount cannot be harmful.

feedback.heading: The verification activity continued unnoticed
feedback.consequence: The attacker may complete the external-account link and prepare a withdrawal.
feedback.explanation: Microdeposits can be verification steps, not gifts or harmless interest.

warningSigns.sign: The source and linked account are unfamiliar.

artifact.callerStatus: Incoming caller; identity not verified; fictional bank name
artifact.heading: The caller asks for the exact deposit amounts
artifact.message: The two small deposits are part of a security check. Please read both amounts to me so I can protect your account.
artifact.transcript: An incoming caller claims to represent the fictional Riverbend Bank and says, "The two small deposits are part of a security check. Please read both amounts to me so I can protect your account." The caller knows that the deposits appeared but has not been independently verified.

scene.question: Would you provide the two amounts?
scene.description: Exact microdeposit amounts may be used to verify control of a linked account.

warningSigns.sign: The call was unexpected.
The caller asks for exact verification amounts.
The caller uses account protection as the reason to complete a verification step.

choice.title: Refuse and call the bank yourself
choice.subtitle: Use a trusted number from the card, statement, or known app.

feedback.heading: You protected the verification values
feedback.consequence: The incoming caller cannot use the learner to confirm the unfamiliar link.
feedback.explanation: Independent bank contact is safer than completing a verification step for someone who called unexpectedly.

warningSigns.sign: The caller needed information only the account holder could see.

choice.title: Ask for a callback number or employee ID
choice.subtitle: Keep the caller engaged while requesting proof.

feedback.heading: The caller supplied convincing but unverified details
feedback.consequence: A polished callback number and employee ID keep the story moving.
feedback.explanation: Information supplied by the caller is not independent verification. End the call and locate the bank yourself.

warningSigns.sign: The person being checked controls the supposed proof.

choice.title: Read both amounts to the caller
choice.subtitle: Provide $0.07 and $0.13 to complete the security check.

feedback.heading: The values may have verified the attacker's account
feedback.consequence: The unfamiliar external link may now be active for money movement.
feedback.explanation: The exact amounts can serve as proof that someone can view the bank account. Do not provide them to an unexpected caller.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested the values immediately after the deposits appeared.

scene.question: What would you do with the unfamiliar link?
scene.description: Do not test an unauthorized payment path with real money.

warningSigns.sign: The institution and masked account are unfamiliar.
The link appeared with unexplained microdeposits.
The learner did not authorize the connection.

choice.title: Lock or remove the link and contact the bank
choice.subtitle: Use available bank controls and request an investigation.

feedback.heading: You interrupted the unauthorized payment path
feedback.consequence: The bank can review how the link was added and whether other access changed.
feedback.explanation: An unknown linked account should be treated as unauthorized until the bank verifies otherwise.

warningSigns.sign: The learner did not create the link.

choice.title: Take a screenshot and wait
choice.subtitle: Preserve the evidence but leave the link active.

feedback.heading: You saved evidence but delayed protection
feedback.consequence: The screenshot may help later, while the external account may still receive a transfer.
feedback.explanation: Preserve the screen and contact the real bank immediately rather than choosing one or the other.

warningSigns.sign: The link can remain usable during the delay.

choice.title: Send a small test transfer
choice.subtitle: Move real money to see where the linked account goes.

feedback.heading: The test moved money to an unauthorized destination
feedback.consequence: The learner confirms the payment path and may suffer an initial loss.
feedback.explanation: Never test an unfamiliar linked account with real money. The bank can investigate it without a customer-initiated payment.

warningSigns.sign: The external recipient is not known or trusted.

artifact.heading: Pending bank-to-bank transfer
artifact.message: An $8,500 ACH transfer is pending to the unfamiliar external account. ACH is a common system for electronic bank-to-bank transfers.
artifact.transcript: The simulated bank screen shows a pending $8,500 ACH transfer to the unrecognized external account. ACH is a common system for electronic bank-to-bank transfers. Pending means the bank must check the current status and what options remain; it does not guarantee that the transfer can be stopped.

scene.question: How would you respond to the pending transfer?
scene.description: Prompt bank contact matters while the transfer is still marked pending.

warningSigns.sign: The learner did not initiate the transfer.
The destination is the unfamiliar linked account.

choice.title: Call the real bank immediately
choice.subtitle: Ask it to review or stop the transfer and secure the account.

feedback.heading: You acted while the transfer was pending

warningSigns.sign: The transfer is unauthorized and may complete soon.

choice.title: Wait until it posts
choice.subtitle: Dispute the transfer only after it completes.

feedback.heading: The pending period passed without a bank request

choice.title: Approve the fake caller's verification request

artifact.heading: Transfer cancellation form
artifact.message: The original caller sends a simulated, nonfunctional page that asks for an online-banking username, password, and security code.

scene.question: Would you use the cancellation form?
scene.description: The form creates a second credential-theft attempt during the transfer emergency.

warningSigns.sign: The page came from the original unverified caller.

choice.title: Ignore the form and stay with the real bank

feedback.heading: You avoided the second credential-theft attempt

artifact.heading: Protect legitimate deposits and payments
artifact.message: Depending on the exposure, the bank may recommend new credentials, stronger authentication, or a replacement account number.
artifact.transcript: The fictional bank may recommend new credentials, stronger authentication, or a replacement account number depending on the exposure. The learner must also protect legitimate Social Security or pension deposits, recurring bills, automatic payments, and approved payees. The bank should guide the transition.

scene.question: How should legitimate activity be handled?
scene.description: A careful inventory prevents the recovery process from disrupting important income and bills.

warningSigns.sign: Rushed changes can interrupt legitimate deposits or payments.
An unrelated new account does not automatically secure the compromised one.

choice.title: Follow the bank's transition plan
choice.subtitle: Update legitimate deposits and payments carefully from a checklist.

feedback.heading: You protected continuity while securing the account
feedback.consequence: Important deposits and bills can move in an organized way if replacement is needed.

warningSigns.sign: Several legitimate services may depend on the current account.

feedback.heading: The account changed, but important items may be missed

warningSigns.sign: Recurring activity is easy to overlook.

choice.title: Open an unrelated account and ignore the original

feedback.heading: The original exposure remained active

feedback.heading: The earliest warning signs would be missed again
feedback.consequence: An attacker may finish verifying another link before a large transfer becomes visible.
feedback.explanation: Unknown microdeposits deserve bank review because their purpose matters more than their size. The ending will retain the earlier consequences instead of converting them into an early-safe result.

warningSigns.sign: The amounts can confirm account access.

artifact.heading: Complete recovery begins after the link progressed
artifact.message: The learner tells the real bank about the amounts, link, transfer, page interaction, and account-access changes and follows a bank-guided transition.
artifact.transcript: The external account and transfer progressed before recovery began. The learner now completes the real bank's review of linked accounts, devices, sessions, profile details, payees, credentials, and transaction status. Recovery is not guaranteed, but further harm may be reduced.

outcome.label: Link progressed; complete recovery started
outcome.heading: You gave the bank the full account-linking timeline
outcome.explanation: The late safe response improves containment while still acknowledging that verification or money movement already advanced.

warningSigns.sign: A later safe choice does not erase the active link or pending transfer.

artifact.heading: The real bank has the complete timeline
artifact.message: You connected the microdeposits, verification call, external link, and transfer, then reviewed access and payment settings together.
artifact.transcript: The learner uses a trusted bank channel, refuses to verify the unfamiliar external account, reports the pending transfer, avoids the fake cancellation form, and completes a broader security review. The bank will determine whether the transfer can be stopped or recovered; no outcome is guaranteed.

outcome.label: Comprehensive response
outcome.heading: You recognized the setup before more money moved
outcome.explanation: Prompt reporting and a full access-and-payment review give the bank the strongest available opportunity to help.

artifact.heading: The transfer was noticed, but the link needs more review
artifact.message: Addressing the large payment helps, but unknown links, devices, sessions, or profile changes may still remain.
artifact.transcript: The learner focuses on the large transfer without fully investigating the account-linking sequence. Contact the real bank through a trusted channel and ask it to review the external account, devices, sessions, profile details, payees, and recent transactions together.

outcome.label: Partial account review
outcome.heading: The immediate warning received attention
outcome.explanation: The response can be strengthened by reviewing how the account was linked and whether other access changed.

artifact.heading: The unauthorized payment path remains a risk
artifact.message: Ignoring microdeposits and linked-account notices can allow a larger transfer to develop unnoticed.
artifact.transcript: The learner treats tiny deposits as harmless while an unfamiliar external link and transfer risk remain. This can happen to anyone. Contact the real bank through a trusted channel immediately, explain the complete sequence, preserve the records, and follow its recovery guidance. Recovery is not guaranteed.

outcome.label: Link risk unresolved
outcome.heading: The early warning signs still matter
outcome.explanation: Acting now can still help secure access and document unauthorized money movement, even if a transfer has already completed.
